45-day holdout explorer

Every hour of the reported holdout, actual against predicted. Six models forecast 24 hours ahead from a fresh origin each night, so the 45 days tile the window exactly once — no overlap, no gaps, and no model ever saw the day it is predicting.

Mon 7 September – Wed 21 October 2026 (45 days) · 24 tanks · 1,080 hourly points per model · point forecasts are raw (uncalibrated), so the six are directly comparable

Window

Hover or focus the chart and use ←/→ to read any point. In the daily view, click a day to open its 24 hours.

Table view — every value on screen ()

How to read it. Each point is a forecast made before the fact: the origin is 23:00 the night before, the horizon is the next 24 hours. Daily points are matched-pair sums — the actual and every prediction are summed over exactly the hours whose meter reading exists — so a partial day cannot flatter one model. Coverage below 100% is called out in the tooltip and in the table; the headline MAE, MAPE and bias skip points under 95% coverage, which is why days with a sensor outage do not count against anyone.

Provenance. Chronos-2 ZS, NPTS, TimesFM 2.5 and Timestral 209M come from results/refresh_2026-10-22/calibrated/predictions_calibrated.parquet; PatchTST from results/refresh_2026-10-22/holdout45_patchtst/predictions_holdout45_patchtst.parquet. All six share the origin grid. The two fitted models (NPTS, PatchTST) share the fit cutoff (2026-09-06 23:00); the three foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM, Timestral) are zero-shot, with their context cut at each origin — so nothing leaks. TimesFM carries the last observed value across a sensor gap that reaches the origin, where Chronos-2 and Timestral mask it. Rebuild with python reports/build_holdout45_page.py.

PatchTST (Mar), dashed, is the published study's holdout PatchTST: fitted to 8 March 2026 on Waltr's figures as they were then, loaded unchanged and run on this window's origins, so it is the one model here whose fit cutoff is not the one above. Its calendar inputs are blank on these dates too, since the calendar ends in May 2026. From results/refresh_2026-10-22/old_vs_new/holdout_old_models.parquet; regenerate with python -m src.models.old_vs_new.

† PatchTST (Sep) is the tuned configuration retrained to 6 Sep 2026 on Waltr's revised, zero-heavy flow figures, without academic-calendar flags for 2024 and after May 2026 — the calendar used here ends in May 2026. In this study it is unstable: in the benchmark the same configuration has a MASE above 1 at all six horizons and forecasts almost nothing at four of them. Read its line as a failed fit, not as evidence about trained models; see results/refresh_2026-10-22/FINAL_ANALYSIS.md and results/refresh_2026-10-22/old_vs_new/OLD_VS_NEW.md.
